paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nobody gets right with God by what they do. Paul says it plainly: "a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ" (Gal 2:16). Not by being born into the right group, not by keeping the right rules, not by the right seat at the right table. If stamping harder could have gotten me out of that junk drawer, I'd have been out in a week.

So why did Paul get so loud with Cephas? Because when Cephas pulled away from the Gentiles, it was out of fear of the circumcision group (Gal 2:12), and Paul said that wasn't "walking in line with the truth of the gospel" (Gal 2:14). The gospel isn't only something we believe. It shapes who we sit with and how we treat people. If Christ is the one who makes us right with God, then nobody gets pushed away from the table for not measuring up to a list.

And here's the part that gets me. Paul says, "I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me" (Gal 2:20). The life he lives, he lives by faith in the Son of God, "who loved me and gave Himself up for me." That's the whole reason this matters to you, baker. You're not working to earn a seat, because you've already been loved, and "if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing" (Gal 2:21).
